cards.explanation: The answer is at ease and secure. Amos says, "Woe to those at ease in Zion and those secure on Mount Samaria…" (Amos 6:1). These folks have settled in so deep they've got dents in the couch, friends.

The answer is, "Are you better than these kingdoms?" Amos asks, "Are you better than these kingdoms? Is their territory larger than yours?" (Amos 6:2). He sends them to Calneh, Hamath and Gath first, so they can look before they answer. I think that's a question you answer a little quieter than you ask it.
The answer is False. The text says they "…bring near a reign of violence." (Amos 6:3). So they dismiss the day of calamity and bring violence near, friends. I think that's a rough trade.

The answer is lambs and stall-fed calves. Amos says, "You dine on lambs from the flock and calves from the stall." (Amos 6:4). That's lamb and calf on the menu while they lounge on ivory beds. Nobody in this scene is eating over the sink, bakers.

The answer is True. Amos says, "You improvise songs on the harp like David and invent your own musical instruments." (Amos 6:5). They play the harp like David, and they invent instruments of their own. That's a lot of creativity, friends.

The answer is grieve. Amos says they drink wine, anoint themselves with the finest oils, "…but you fail to grieve over the ruin of Joseph." (Amos 6:6). The wine and the oil sit in the same verse as the failure to grieve. Grief is the thing missing, friends.

The answer is into exile as the first captives. Amos says, "Therefore, you will now go into exile as the first of the captives, and your feasting and lounging will come to an end." (Amos 6:7). It's a hard turn, friends. The ones who were lounging are named the first of the captives.

The answer is pride. The Lord GOD declares, "I abhor Jacob’s pride and detest his citadels…" (Amos 6:8). He swore it by Himself, which is as serious as it gets. I think that fits with the folks who said they took Karnaim by their own strength.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "…so I will deliver up the city and everything in it." (Amos 6:8). Everything in it, friends, not just a piece. He sets that right after naming Jacob's pride and citadels.

The answer is None. The relative asks, "Is anyone else with you?" and the person answers, "None" (Amos 6:10). I think this part hurts to read, so let's take it gently, friends. It shows how complete things have become.

The answer is False. The relative retorts, "Silence," and gives this reason: "for the name of the LORD must not be invoked." (Amos 6:10). It's the opposite of calling on the name, friends. This is a heavy scene, so we'll let it sit.

The answer is False. The command covers both: "The great house will be smashed to pieces, and the small house to rubble." (Amos 6:11). The small house doesn't get a pass, friends. It's a serious verse, and it names both sizes on purpose.

The answer is that they turned justice into poison. The LORD says, "But you have turned justice into poison and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood…" (Amos 6:12). That's two turnarounds in one verse, friends. Justice into poison, and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood.
The answer is by our own strength. They say, "Did we not take Karnaim by our own strength?" (Amos 6:13). Notice who gets the credit in that sentence, friends. It's all "we" and "our own."

The answer is nation. The LORD says, "For behold, I will raise up a nation against you, O house of Israel…" (Amos 6:14). It's the God of Hosts speaking, and He's talking straight to Israel. The text doesn't name that nation here, friends.
